1.21.1.0.577.0:
### 0.577.0

**Fortresses and bastions in the Nether**

The Nether crossing is no longer empty country. Nether fortresses, bastion remnants, nether fossils and ruined portals now generate out there — the real ones, with their own loot, their blaze spawners and wither skeleton halls, their piglin brutes and Pigstep. Fortresses stand on their own bridge supports over the lava, and where one happens to lie across the line, the train tunnels straight through it.

- Nether fortresses generate in the Nether crossing, with blazes, wither skeletons and their loot
- Bastion remnants, complete with piglin brutes, treasure rooms and the netherite upgrade template
- Nether fossils in soul sand valleys, and ruined portals with their blackstone and loot
- Ride straight through a fortress that lands across the tracks
1.21.1.0.576.0:
### 0.576.0

**Saving in the editor no longer re-mirrors your build**

Hitting Save in an in-game editor used to rebuild the mirrored half of the plot from the master octant first, quietly overwriting anything you had deliberately made asymmetric — and anything placed by a route the live mirror doesn't watch, like a clipboard paste or an edit made before you turned the axis on. Save now captures the plot exactly as you left it. When you do want the far half rebuilt from the master, ask for it: the new Mirror -> Rebuild button in the editor menu, or /dungeontrain editor mirror rebuild.

- Save captures the plot as it stands — mirroring no longer runs behind your back
- New on-demand re-mirror: Mirror -> Rebuild in the editor menu, or /dungeontrain editor mirror rebuild
- Live mirroring while you build is unchanged
1.21.1.0.575.0:
### 0.575.0

**Better review for player translation fixes**

When you correct a machine-translated string in the in-game translation editor, your client now also reports the AI text you replaced. The reviewer sees your fix side by side with the original instead of on its own, so genuine corrections are easier to tell apart and quicker to approve.
1.21.1.0.574.0:
### 0.574.0

**Nether lava fix**

Lava in the Nether band now behaves the way it should.

### 0.573.0

**New dimensional carriages by Lil Detective Crunch**

Two new dimensional carriages built by Lil Detective Crunch now ride the train, one of them stocked with nether-themed loot and mobs.

- Two new dimensional carriages by Lil Detective Crunch

### 0.572.0

**Two new Train Dimension rooms**

Two more rooms can turn up behind a Train Dimension portal. One is a trap room, sealed on every side in bedrock. The other is a parkour room with nothing around it at all - no walls, no shell, just empty space out past the fog. Both start showing up from level 10, and both are uncommon, so the rooms you already know still make up most of what you walk into.

- New trap room, sealed all the way round in bedrock
- New parkour room, hanging in open space with no shell around it
- Both appear from level 10 onward

### 0.571.0

**Portal rooms can be one author's library**

A portal room can now be a single community author's library. Its bookshelves are stocked with that person's whole catalogue and every shelf past the end of it is left empty, so a hall of bare shelves with a dozen books in it tells you exactly how much they wrote. The room announces whose library you have walked into.

- New Books setting on portal rooms in the editor: off, or an author mix.
- The room rolls between your own writing and somebody else's, and each room sets its own odds — a study can lean toward your own shelves while a great hall leans toward strangers.
- Rooms can ask for a particular kind of author: at least this many books written, and at most that many, so a modest private collection stays modest.
- Written nothing yourself? The room quietly picks somebody else rather than standing empty.
1.21.1.0.570.0:
### 0.569.0

**The house — a player-built room**

Built in the Train Editor by Twitch streamer xxx606xxx_, and the first player-made package to ship with Dungeon Train.

### 0.568.0

**The train tells you when a book went unsigned**

Shelve a book & quill you wrote in but never signed, and a quiet line tells you the train won't carry it. Signing is what sends a book out into the world — an unsigned one just sits on the shelf, and now the game says so instead of leaving you guessing.

- Putting a written-in but unsigned book & quill into a chiseled bookshelf shows one of five lines
- Nothing else changes: the book still goes on the shelf and can be taken back out
1.21.1.0.567.0:
### 0.567.0

**Debug command menu is creative-only**

The X debug/command menu no longer opens outside creative mode. Shift+X previously bypassed the creative gate and opened it in survival; that override is gone, and the menu now closes itself if you drop out of creative while it is open.

- X and Shift+X no longer open the debug menu in survival
- The menu closes automatically when you leave creative

**Train engine volume slider**

The train's engine loop now has its own volume, so you can turn the train down without turning the whole world's ambience down with it. It sits in Options > Music & Sounds beside the other volumes, and is repeated in Options > Dungeon Train and the in-world X menu. Sliding it to OFF stops the engine entirely; everything else about how the sound behaves - loudest in a carriage, fading out as you walk away, quiet in a Train Dimension room - is unchanged, just quieter or louder overall.

- New Dungeon Train Engine volume slider in Options > Music & Sounds
- Separate from the Ambient slider, so cave and mob sounds keep their own level
- OFF silences the engine completely
1.21.1.0.566.0:
### 0.566.0

**Train Dimension loot now matches its carriage**

Chests inside a Train Dimension now roll their loot to the stage of the portal carriage you walked in through, so they're worth what a carriage's chests are worth at that point in the run. Which room you get, and how it is built, is unchanged.

- Train Dimension room loot now scales to the portal carriage you entered from
- Enchantment levels in those rooms are capped to the run's progression again
1.21.1.0.565.0:
### 0.565.0

**Sealed Train Dimensions are properly sealed**

The bedrock around a sealed Train Dimension now covers its hallways and end faces too, instead of stopping at the room — so there is no longer a wall you can mine through to get out.
1.21.1.0.564.0:
### 0.564.0

**Train Dimensions: improvements to the lost-train fix**

Improves the recent fix for a Train Dimension losing its train: being put back on board no longer hurts you, and it asks less of the game while it finds the way back.
1.21.1.0.563.0:
### 0.563.0

**Train Dimensions: fixed rooms losing their train**

Fixes the way a Train Dimension could lose the carriages it belongs to while you were still inside it, leaving you sealed in a room whose corridors led nowhere. The room now keeps hold of its part of the train for as long as you are in there — and in the unlikely event it loses it anyway, you are put back on the train instead of left with no way out.

- Fixed a room losing its train while you were inside it
- Fixed being left with no way out when it happened — you are returned to the train instead
- Untested in multiplayer — how this behaves with several players on one train is not yet known
1.21.1.0.562.0:
### 0.562.0

**Train Dimensions: the way back always works**

Every corridor in a Train Dimension now takes you back aboard — the one you came in through and the extra ways out scattered deep in the room — however long you stay or how far you wander. Before, a room you had gone far enough into could quietly lose its train, leaving you sealed in with nowhere left to walk.

- Corridor copies deep in an endless room always lead back to the train
- No more getting stranded in a Train Dimension you walked too far into
- Untested in multiplayer — how this behaves with several players on one train is not yet known
1.21.1.0.561.0:
### 0.561.0

**Portal-side carriages hang together**

Blocks in the portal-side carriages no longer each pick their own look in isolation — some of them now follow the carriage's stonework, so a run of wall or floor reads as one surface instead of a patchwork. Which blocks follow and which stay independent varies per carriage, so the effect changes as you ride.

- Portal-side contents now share their look between blocks rather than rolling each one separately
1.21.1.0.560.0:
### 0.560.0

**Shorter portal carriages, and a seamless crossing**

Portal corridors now come in two lengths. Alongside the long corridor that stretches into the carriage behind it, there is a new one exactly the size of an ordinary carriage — and each portal on the train picks between them, so they no longer all feel the same. Crossing one is smoother too: the door ahead of you is always a real one, changing your mind partway along works, and standing in a doorway never moves you.

- A new carriage-length portal corridor, with its own interior and ten furnishing variants
- Roughly half of the portals you meet are the new shorter kind
- Change your mind partway along a portal corridor and walk straight back out onto the train
- The door in front of you is always one that opens — no more walking into a dead one
- Standing in a portal doorway no longer moves you
1.21.1.0.559.0:
### 0.559.0

**Ride photos for building in a drifting carriage, and for arriving in a Train Dimension**

The camera that quietly takes photos of your run now watches for two more moments. Leave your marks on a drifting carriage — somebody else's build that has come to your train — and it takes a photo of the work. Walk a hallway portal and stay a while in the room on the other side, and it takes a wide shot of wherever you have ended up. Both turn up in your gallery and on the death screen with the rest of the run. The Train Dimension photo waits until you have actually walked in and looked around, so it shows the room rather than the doorway, and it is framed to stay inside the room you are standing in rather than the identical one next door.

- New photo taken when you build in a drifting carriage
- New photo taken once you have arrived inside a Train Dimension
- Train Dimension photos are framed from inside the room you are in, never from the copy next door or from inside a corridor
1.21.1.0.558.0:
### 0.558.0

**Armor stands you place on a train now stay with the train**

Placing an armor stand inside a carriage used to look like nothing happened — the stand really was created, but it ended up in the carriage's internal building space rather than on the train you were standing on, where nobody could ever see it. Placed stands now ride the carriage they were put on, staying put as the train moves and surviving a reload.

- Armor stands can be placed and displayed inside carriages
- Placed stands stay locked to their carriage while the train moves
- They survive carriage unloading and world reload
1.21.1.0.557.0:
### 0.557.0

**Help Translate on the Ways to Help page**

If you play Dungeon Train in a language that was machine-translated, the Ways to Help page now offers you the translation editor directly - so fixing the lines that read wrong sits alongside donating, sharing and feedback as a way to help. The page also scrolls now, and its Done button stays put at the bottom instead of sliding off the edge of a small window.

- New "Help Translate" section on the Ways to Help page, shown when your language still has AI-translated lines nobody has reviewed
- The Ways to Help page scrolls, and Done is pinned to the bottom so it can never be pushed off-screen

**Video Tools page for content creators**

A new Video Tools button on the title menu, for anyone filming Dungeon Train. Each of the two filming commands gets a tile playing a clip of what it actually looks like — cinematographer mode, which flies you through the train in spectator with every door swinging open ahead of you, and the intro cinematic, which you can replay from anywhere in a run. Click a tile for the full rundown. The page also points you at #streams-and-media-of-dungeontrain to share what you make, and at the dev if you need a hand with a shot.

- New Video Tools page on the title menu, with an animated tile per filming command
- /dt cinematographer — spectator flight with auto-opening doors (including on the moving train), an adjustable door radius, and clear-view for shots through walls
- /dt cinematic — replay the intro cinematic from anywhere, or press C in spectator
- Flags that cinematographer mode puts the run into Free Play, while replaying the cinematic does not
- Discord moves to a logomark button above Credits, freeing its old slot for Video Tools
1.21.1.0.556.0:
### 0.556.0

**Train Dimensions — doors on the train that open somewhere else**

Somewhere past your first stretch of track, a corridor between two carriages stops being a corridor. Walk it and the sound of the train falls away behind you, and you come out in a room that could never have fitted inside the carriage you stepped into — a hall, a library, a place of beams and sculk, some of them going on for as long as you care to keep walking. What you find is drawn from how far you have come, so late portals open onto places the early ones never do, and every portal rolls its own room: chests you loot stay looted when you walk back in. The train keeps rolling while you look around, and the ground you cover in there counts toward your journey. Nothing strands you — there is always a way back out — and if you would rather the door weren't there at all, breaking through the corridor's outer wall closes that portal for good.

**Editor: middle-click copies a cell's block variants**

In the block-variant editor, middle-clicking a cell that has variants now puts that cell's whole variant list in your hand as a clipboard item — no opening the Z menu, no hunting through your backpack for it. If the same clipboard is already on your hotbar it just switches to that slot, and middle-clicking anything else still does a normal pick-block.

- Middle-click a variant cell to copy it straight to your hotbar
- Switches to the matching clipboard when you already have one
- Vanilla pick-block still works on every other block

**Resizing a portal room now grows it from both ends**

In the room editor, the length and width steppers alternate which wall moves, so a room grows outwards from what you have built instead of always off the far end. Shrinking is no longer one-way: the row you crop is remembered for this world, and stepping the size back up puts those blocks, their variants and their chest contents back exactly as they were. Resizing also keeps whatever you have built since your last save, and Reset now puts a room's dimensions back along with its blocks.

- Length and width grow and shrink from alternating ends; height still moves only its ceiling
- A row removed by shrinking comes back if you grow the room again
- Resizing no longer discards edits made since your last save
- Reset restores the saved size, not just the saved blocks

**Villagers price up the item you are holding**

Updated the bundled Trade Everything mod. A villager's Trade Anything slot now cycles through what it will take and previews the price for the item you are currently holding, so you can see what a trade is worth before you make it.

- Held-item price preview in the Trade Anything slot
- Cycling Trade Anything icon

**More variety in one of the small path rooms**

A pass over the pathssmall portal room: more of its blocks now vary between copies, and more of its containers roll from curated pools, so repeat visits look and loot differently.

### 0.555.0

**Difficulty set by command no longer follows you into a new world or a new life**

Setting the difficulty by command — /dungeontrain difficulty, or the difficulty /dtp applies when it drops you somewhere far down the line — used to be written once and left everywhere: start a brand-new world and it opened at whatever tier you last set, and dying didn't undo it either, so a fresh run carried on at a difficulty it never earned. That setting now belongs to the world you set it in. A new world starts on automatic, dying puts you back on automatic, and the world you set it in still remembers it when you come back.

- A newly created world no longer inherits a difficulty set in another world
- Dying resets the difficulty back to automatic — the new run scales from real travel again
- Reloading the world you set it in keeps the difficulty you set
- On a server with other players still riding, one player's death leaves the difficulty alone

### 0.554.0

**Each difficulty is now its own run**

Peaceful, Easy, Normal and Hard each keep their own gear, XP, Ender Chest and echoes. Switch difficulty and you switch profiles — what you were carrying is waiting for you when you switch back, and nothing you farmed on an easier setting comes with you.

- Your Ender Chest is now per-difficulty, and so is the inventory and XP carried between runs when keepInventory is on.
- An Ender Chest that isn't your default one says so in its title — "Ender Chest (Hard)", "(Adventure · Hard)" or "(Free Play)" — so an empty chest never looks like lost items.
- Echoes only return on the difficulty they died on, so a Hard run never meets a Peaceful ghost.
- Changing difficulty in-game tells you in chat which profile you moved to and where your gear is waiting.
- Normal keeps everything you already have — existing Ender Chests and past lives all belong to Normal, so nothing goes missing.

**The rooms beyond the corridors count toward your journey, and two new advancements**

Step through a carriage corridor into one of the rooms that could never fit inside it and the train keeps rolling without you — but until now, everything you travelled while you were in there counted for nothing. It counts now: you cover as much ground as the train does while you look around. Two new advancements come with it, one for going inside at all, and one for finding your way out somewhere far from where you came in.

- Time and distance now keep counting while you are inside one of the impossible rooms
- New advancement: 'Train inside a train?' for stepping out of a corridor into a room that could never have fitted in the carriage
- New advancement: 'A new way out' for leaving one of those rooms by a corridor at least 50 blocks from the one you entered through

**A broken portal can be walked through, and portals stop failing silently**

Breaking open a portal corridor's shell still closes the portal for good, but the pair no longer leaves three carriages of dead end behind it: the blocks between its two doors are removed, so you can walk straight through the group and carry on down the train. Separately, a portal you lingered in could quietly stop working — its destination was left behind as the train rolled on, and walking past the midpoint then did nothing at all. It now keeps up with you.

- A severed portal opens into a walk-through instead of a dead end
- Portals no longer stop working if you linger in the corridor before crossing

### 0.553.0

**The death screen recap now works in multiplayer**

Dying on a server used to give you Minecraft's plain death screen. Now you get the same end-of-run recap singleplayer gets — your fall, your deeds, your cargo, your ride photos and the rest — with Respawn in place of the board-a-new-train button, since a server world isn't yours to restart.

- The narrative death screen now appears on LAN and dedicated servers
- Respawn replaces Board anew there, and the delete-world toggle is hidden

### 0.552.0

**Portal rooms stop breaking their own furnishings**

Furnishing a portal room knocked loose whatever was resting on the floor it was decorating. The single-pillar room showed it worst: the ring of pressure plates around the pillar was broken off and left lying on the floor as items, every time, alongside a fresh set of plates. Rooms are now furnished without disturbing anything standing on them.

- Portal rooms no longer scatter broken pieces of their own furnishings across the floor
- Furnishing a room takes half the block updates it used to

**More ways out of an endless portal room**

The rooms behind a portal that repeat forever used to have exactly one way back to the train, however far you wandered. They can now scatter extra corridors through themselves, so there is usually another way out somewhere near you. Walk back in through one and you return to where you left, rather than to the start. Some rooms hide the way onward as well: the door directly opposite the one you arrived by may be nothing but more room, and the real one is somewhere else in the maze. Corridor doorways are also built from the room's own walls now, instead of the slab of polished blackstone they used to bring with them.

- Endless portal rooms scatter extra ways back to the train
- Walking back in returns you to the corridor you came out of, not to the start
- Some rooms stand their way onward somewhere other than directly opposite
- Corridor doorways are built from the room's own walls, not polished blackstone
- Portal rooms no longer spill the contents of their bookshelves and chests onto the floor

**Portal room furnishings are curated, and their mobs scale with difficulty**

Furnished portal rooms now draw from a curated set of furnishings instead of anything the train could offer, so a window room reads as a window room. The default portal room's mobs now scale with the run: low difficulties meet zombies, while witches, vindicators and pillagers only start appearing as the difficulty climbs. Furnishings built for portal rooms no longer turn up in ordinary train carriages.

- Portal room mobs scale with difficulty - zombies early, witches and vindicators later
- Furnished portal rooms draw from a curated set of furnishings
- Portal-only furnishings no longer appear in ordinary carriages
- Window portal rooms now use the bedrock-lock layout

**Portal doorways stay with their carriage instead of being left behind**

A portal's doorway belongs to the carriage carrying it. If that carriage was set aside while the train rolled on, the doorway could be left behind hanging where the train used to be — and riding an ordinary carriage through that spot would pull you in and drop you into the empty space beneath the world, without you ever having walked into a portal. A doorway now travels with its carriage or stops existing entirely, and a portal that has nowhere solid on the other side quietly does nothing instead of dropping you.

- Riding an ordinary carriage can no longer pull you through a portal you never walked into
- A portal with nowhere solid to land now does nothing rather than dropping you below the world

**Portals stay out of your opening carriages**

Hallway portals no longer turn up in the first stretch of the train. Nothing before difficulty level 2 — around sixty carriages in — holds a portal, so you get to know the train before something that plainly isn't part of it opens up in the middle of it. Past that point portals arrive on their usual sporadic cadence, counted from where they start rather than from the station, so the first one doesn't keep you waiting twice.

- Portals no longer generate before difficulty level 2 (~60 carriages in)
- The first portal past that point arrives on the normal cadence, not after a second wait

### 0.539.0

**Breaking into a portal corridor closes it for good**

Dig through the outer wall of a portal corridor past the halfway point and the portal breaks — glass shatters, a beacon dies away, and that portal never takes you through again. You can always still walk back out of a portal room, so a broken portal can strand nothing and nobody.

- Breaking a portal corridor's outer wall past the halfway point permanently closes it
- Both ends of a portal close together — one hole shuts the whole thing
- The way back out always works, so you can never be trapped in a portal room
- Digging inside a portal room, or before the halfway point, is safe

**Portal transitions no longer flash**

Stepping through a portal corridor used to flash the world for a moment on the other side — sometimes a wash of pale sky, sometimes the skybox showing through where the room should be. The arrival is now drawn properly, so walking a portal looks like walking through a doorway.

- No flash on arriving in a portal room, in either direction
- Endless portal rooms no longer white out as their fog comes in

**Portal rooms can hold enemies, and no two corridors are alike**

Step through a portal and the corridor you walk isn't always the same one — each portal furnishes its own. The pocket room beyond can be home to something, too: rooms are authored with the creatures that live in them, and an endless room keeps them coming as it unfolds around you.

- Portal rooms can be home to creatures, placed by whoever built the room
- Each portal's corridors are furnished from their own set, so no two portals read the same

**The void around a bedrockless portal room closes in as you walk out**

Some portal rooms are built standing in empty space rather than sealed in rock. Walking off one of those and out into the emptiness used to look exactly like standing still in it — the same haze at every distance. The fog now thickens the further out you get, until the room you left has vanished and the dark has no edge you can find.

- Fog closes in progressively as you walk away from a bedrockless portal room
- Walk far enough and the room behind you disappears entirely
- Fixed: the fog used to cut out the moment you stepped off the structure, instead of thickening

**Portal rooms no longer fill up with broken blocks and doubled-up mobs**

A portal's room was being torn down and rebuilt over and over as the train rolled, instead of being built once. Every rebuild left the room a little more cluttered: pressure plates popped off their supports and their drops stayed floating where they broke, and the room's own mobs were carried over and then spawned again beside themselves. A room is now laid down once, and stays as it was built.

- Fixed: floating dropped items piling up in portal rooms, where blocks had been broken by a rebuild
- Fixed: a portal room's mobs appearing twice over, growing every time the train travelled
- Portal rooms are built once instead of being repeatedly re-laid as the train moves

**The music fades out as you walk into a portal**

Head down a portal corridor and the soundtrack sinks away with every step, gone by the time you reach the door. Portal rooms are silent — nothing plays in there, however long you stay. Walk back out onto the train and the music doesn't come blaring back mid-song either; the quiet holds for a while, then a fresh track starts on its own.

- Music fades out over the last stretch of a portal corridor
- Portal rooms are completely silent
- No jarring mid-track resume when you come back to the train

**Walking through a portal no longer counts as leaving the train**

Stepping through a hallway portal used to look, to the game, exactly like jumping off the side of the train — so a walk to a portal room and back handed out Off the Rails and Back on Board for using a door. Those awards, and the one for shoving a passenger off the train, now ignore everything that happens beneath the world's bedrock, which is where portal rooms are built. Leaving the train the honest way still earns them, and shoving an echo into the void still earns Into the Void.

- Portal trips no longer award Off the Rails or Back on Board
- Leading a punched passenger through a portal no longer counts as shoving them off the train
- Genuinely leaving the train, and voiding an echo, still earn their advancements

**The endless portal rooms now carry on past their tunnels**

In an endless portal room, the tunnels back to the train stand inside the room rather than at its edge — but the ground gave out around them. Walk round the side of one and the floor simply stopped: open void, with the tunnel hanging in it. The room now continues past its tunnels, laying its own floor, ceiling and walls right up to them, so a tunnel reads as something standing in the hall that you can walk around. Open-walled endless rooms carry their floor and ceiling through in the same way.

- Fixed: void where the floor should be, in the aisles either side of a portal room's tunnels
- An endless room's own walls and ceiling now continue around its tunnels
- The way back to the train is still a wall with a door in it, unchanged

**Monsters no longer spawn in the empty dark below the world**

Portal rooms are built in an empty basement beneath the world's bedrock, and the game still treated that space as somewhere ordinary monsters could turn up — on a room's roof, in the gap just outside its walls, or anywhere else down there the dark reached. Nothing arrives on its own below the bedrock now. The mobs a portal room is built with are unaffected, and so is anything you bring down there yourself.

- Fixed: skeletons and zombies gathering around portal rooms, below the world's bedrock
- Nothing spawns of its own accord beneath the bedrock layer
- A portal room's own mobs, and any you lead in yourself, are untouched

**Nothing generates in the empty space beneath the world**

The space under the world's bedrock is kept clear for portal rooms, but structures anchored at a fixed depth — trial chambers, ancient cities — were resolving into it and building there anyway: sealed beneath the bedrock, impossible to reach, and pointed at by /locate as though you could go and find them. Nothing generates below the bedrock now, and a structure that straddles it keeps only the part that reaches real ground.

- Fixed: trial chambers and ancient cities generating below the world's bedrock, out of reach
- /locate no longer sends you after a structure buried under the bedrock
- The space beneath the bedrock stays clear for portal rooms

**Cave noises carry through the portal rooms**

A portal room is meant to feel a long way from the train: the soundtrack fades out as you walk the tunnel and there is none at all once you are inside. That left the rooms completely silent, which read as nothing there rather than somewhere else. The old familiar cave noises now turn up while you are in a portal room — the same distant groans and drips you get deep underground, drifting in from somewhere past the walls every half-minute to a few minutes. They stop at the room: the tunnels back to the train still carry the engine and the last of the music, and nothing follows you back aboard.

- Cave noises now play while you are inside a portal room
- They come and go on their own, roughly every 30 seconds to 3 minutes
- The tunnels back to the train are unchanged — engine and fading music as before
- Controlled by the Ambient volume slider, like cave noises anywhere else

**Every portal room is its own room**

Portal rooms all looked the same. Two portals that drew the same kind of room were identical down to the block — same walls, same chests, same contents — so the tenth portal you walked was the first one again. Each portal now rolls its own room, from where it sits on the train. Walk back into one you've already been through and it is still the room you left, chests and all.

- Each portal's room rolls its own blocks, chests and furnishings
- Rooms you have already looted stay looted when you walk back in

**Portal rooms are themed to how far you have travelled**

The room behind a portal is no longer drawn from the whole pool every time. Each room — and each of its sub-variants — can now be limited to a stretch of the run, so early portals open onto different places than late ones. Comes with a batch of authored rooms: a new zombie room, furnished starting rooms with loot chests and mobs, and reworked beam and sculk rooms.

- Portal rooms are drawn to match your progress through the run
- New zombie portal room
- The starting portal rooms are furnished with loot chests, mobs and more block variety
- Reworked beam and sculk rooms
1.21.1.0.552.0:
### 0.552.0

**Mod recommendations now come after the support page**

On the death screen, the page asking which of your other mods you'd recommend now appears after the support page, just before you board again. Same pages, new order.

- Mod recommendations moved after 'support the line'

**Fix your language's own text, from inside the game**

Dungeon Train speaks nineteen languages besides English, and most of those lines were written by a machine. If one of them reads wrong to you, you can now fix it yourself: Options → Language → Help Translate opens the mod's whole vocabulary, line by line, with the English original beside each one and your language's current wording ready to edit. Send your fixes in and, once a human has read them, they reach everyone playing in that language — no update to install. Your name goes on them in the credits, unless you would rather it did not.

- Help Translate sits on the language screen, and on the title screen beside the language button
- Every line the mod ships, with filters for what a human has never checked
- Work in a batch and send it when it is ready — nothing leaves the game until you press Submit
- Approved fixes arrive when the game starts or you change language
- A fix applies to the version it was written against and later ones, so an old fix never overwrites newer wording
- Export and import the files if you would rather work outside the game

**Carriages you've walked away from stop running their mobs**

A long train used to keep every mob in every carriage you had already passed thinking at full speed, forever. Now, once every player has been more than 55 blocks from a carriage for a few seconds, that carriage's mobs are set aside — and restored the moment someone comes back, exactly as you left them: villager trades, gear, inventories, names and positions all intact. Half-loot a carriage, wander off, come back, and you'll find what you left rather than a fresh roll. This mostly helps dedicated servers and multiplayer, where mobs on carriages nobody is near were pure overhead. You may occasionally spot mobs in a far-off carriage blink out and reappear as you get closer; that's this at work.

**New "Dungeon Train (Flat)" world type**

Creating a world now offers "Dungeon Train (Flat)" alongside the usual Dungeon Train option. The train runs across level ground with no terrain generation at all, which makes it a calm place to build, test contraptions, or just watch the train without the landscape getting in the way. One thing to know before you pick it: because nothing is generated around the track, the shifting terrain bands don't appear either — no disintegration stretch and no Nether transition. Choose the normal Dungeon Train world type if you want those.

**Love Notes — an echo that comes back loving you**

The Death Note has a mirror. Sign a book titled "Love Note" naming another player and it burns away in pink flame instead of soul-fire. When you later die, an echo of you waits for them at the carriage depth you fell at — and greets them instead of hunting them.
